registers.role: controls / sample frame: labour market status, occupation (4-digit ISCO codes), demographics
controls: family ties, parental and single-parent status
controls / subsample definition: highest completed educational degree
outcomes: purchases of prescription drugs by drug type (ATC codes); antidepressants are ATC N06 A
controls / sample frame: sales, employment, industry codes
controls: capital stock of all firms
treatment: all import and export transactions by 6-digit HS product code and origin or destination country
treatment (extension): employment, sales and host country of all foreign subsidiaries of Danish firms
linkage: consistent links between individuals and firms

registers.name_in_paper: Trade Council caseworker call data (obtained from the Trade Council, Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
registers.role: treatment (robustness): firm ID, caseworker host country and year of each call

registers.name_in_paper: World Economic Forum Gender Gap Index (Hausmann et al., 2007)
registers.role: controls (robustness): gender attitudes in partner countries, 128 countries
moderator: five occupational characteristics limiting temporal flexibility (Goldin, 2014), linked to ISCO occupation codes

linkages: Individuals are identified in all registers by the same personal ID code, which allows the individual-level data to be merged
Firms are identified in all registers by the same firm ID code
Consistent links between individuals and firms are obtained from the FIDA database
Individuals are linked through family ties in the family and household register (FAM)
O*NET occupational characteristics are linked to ISCO occupation codes
Trade Council caseworker calls are matched to firms by firm ID, country and year

sample.universe: Matched worker-firm data for 2008-2017 for the universe of firms in the private sector in Denmark; the regression sample is restricted to workers aged 20-60 in Danish manufacturing firms with more than 10 employees that both import and export
selection_rules: Period 2008-2017 (FATO affiliate data only 2010-2017; Trade Council call analysis 2008-2015; exit outcomes 2008-2016)
Private-sector firms in Denmark; manufacturing only in the regression sample
Firms with more than 10 employees (a firm with fewer than 10 in a single year but more than 10 in the adjacent years is kept for that year)
Firms that both export and import
Observations with bho = 0 dropped by the log transformation (0.02% of observations)
sample.n_observations: just under 2 million worker-year observations from approximately 3400 unique firms; Table 1 reports 1,987,066 worker-year observations (356,405 college men, 1,005,479 non-college men, 220,488 college women, 404,694 non-college women)
sample.n_individuals: 97,569 women and 218,198 men in the full-sample baseline specification (Table 2, Panel A, column 1)

construction_notes: bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and country d|, 0}: the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and partner country d (Eq. 1)
bho^trade_jt: firm-level average of bho_d weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations (Eq. 2)
bho^Affiliates_jt: firm-level average of bho_d weighted by the number of the firm's foreign affiliates in each destination (Eq. 3); set to 8 for firms with no foreign affiliates
bho enters the regressions in logs, which drops 0.02% of the sample observations
Antidepressant use: indicator for any purchase of a drug with ATC code N06 A in a given year
Parental status: having a child younger than 19 living at home (the control in Eq. (4) is an indicator for having children younger than 25 living at home)
Single parent: an adult living with their own child under 19 but not living with a non-related adult with a less than 15-year age difference

Gender Gap Index: World Economic Forum index for 2007, averaged for each firm weighted by product-destination country combinations; a time-varying version uses the closest available value in each year (Table C.3)

O*NET measure: average of Time Pressure, Contact with others, Structured versus Unstructured Work, Freedom to Make Decisions and Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships, standardized on the full sample; assigned by the worker's FIRST reported occupation (4-digit), with a within-spell varying variant in Table C.5; D() denotes an indicator for being above the 75th percentile
Education fixed effects have 12 levels; occupational fixed effects are based on 2-digit ISCO codes
Exit outcomes are dummies defined in year t by observing the worker in t+1
Standard errors are clustered at the firm level throughout

claims.statement: A lower business hours overlap between a Danish manufacturing firm and its foreign trading partners does not raise the use of prescription antidepressants among its female workers relative to its male workers in the full sample of workers aged 20-60.

register_source.value: UH (foreign trade statistics register): all import and export transactions by 6-digit HS product code and partner country; worker-firm links from FIDA

definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. Logs are taken in estimation, which drops 0.02% of observations. A LOWER bho means a greater need to work outside standard Danish business hours.

timing.value: Firm's business hours overlap in the same year t as the outcome

outcome.label: Indicator variable indicating if the individual has purchased antidepressants in a given year

register_source.value: LMDB (prescription drugs register): purchases of prescription drugs by drug type (ATC codes); antidepressants = ATC N06 A

definition.value: Dummy equal to one if worker i purchased prescription antidepressant medication (ATC code N06 A) in year t, zero otherwise. Taken from the comprehensive prescription drugs register, which records all purchases of prescription drugs by drug type. Used as a proxy for mental well-being; Danish health care is free and universal, so access is not correlated with income or employment status.

timing.value: Purchases during year t, the same year as the firm's business hours overlap

units.value: change in the probability of purchasing antidepressants in a year (probability points, outcome is a 0/1 indicator) for women relative to men, per one unit of ln(business hours overlap); the paper notes ln(8)-ln(3) is approximately 1, so the coefficient is approximately the effect of a five-hour fall in overlap from 8 to 3 h

estimand.target_population: The difference between female and male workers employed by the same firm in the same year, within the estimation subsample (a gender-differential effect, not a level effect for women)
estimand.time_horizon: Contemporaneous: antidepressant purchases in the same calendar year as the measured business hours overlap
estimand.formal_query: {E[Y | do(ln bho = b'), Female=1] - E[Y | do(ln bho = b), Female=1]} - {E[Y | do(ln bho = b'), Female=0] - E[Y | do(ln bho = b), Female=0]}, per unit b'-b, within firm-year cells

population.description: All workers aged 20-60 in Danish manufacturing firms that export and import and have more than 10 employees, 2008-2017
subgroups_defined: single parents vs cohabiting parents vs employees without children
occupations above vs below the 75th percentile of the Goldin (2014) O*NET index
population.selection: Worker-year observations of workers aged 20-60 employed in Danish private-sector manufacturing firms that both export and import and have more than 10 employees (a firm with fewer than 10 employees in a single year but more than 10 in the adjacent years is kept); the sample covers 81% of Danish manufacturing employment and 98% of Danish manufacturing exports. Estimation with job-spell fixed effects uses only workers observed in the same worker-firm match in more than one year.

identification.source_of_variation: Variation over time in the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap with its foreign buyers and suppliers WITHIN a given worker-firm (job) spell, combined with the contrast between female and male workers employed by the same firm in the same year

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditional on worker-firm spell, firm-year, female-year, occupation, occupation-female and education fixed effects and on experience, experience squared and having children, within-spell changes in the firm's business hours overlap are unrelated to other determinants of the female-male difference in antidepressant use
key_assumptions.supported_by: Identification discussion in Section 3 (two pillars: job-spell fixed effects and the within-firm-year female-male contrast); the authors state that holding the worker-firm match fixed and controlling for firm-year fixed effects rules out self-selection of workers into firms and of healthier firms into internationalization

implies_edges.from: time-invariant worker and worker-firm match heterogeneity (pre-natal and early-life environment, genetic differences)
firm-year unobservables (drivers of internationalization, corporate culture, average stress, demand and productivity shocks)
gender-specific year effects (differential propensity to use antidepressants over time)

key_assumptions.assumption: Any reverse causality running from the mental well-being of a firm's workforce to the firm's internationalization (and hence its business hours overlap) operates at the firm-year level and is therefore absorbed by firm-year fixed effects
key_assumptions.supported_by: Argued in Section 3 and in Section 5.2, citing Eaton et al. (2011) on more productive firms serving more distant markets

implies_edges.from: workforce mental well-being and firm productivity

key_assumptions.assumption: Conditioning the estimation on observed job spells does not select the sample: workers' exit from the firm or from the sample does not respond differentially by gender to changes in the business hours overlap

definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. Logs are taken in estimation, which drops 0.02% of observations. A LOWER bho means a greater need to work outside standard Danish business hours.

definition.value: Dummy equal to one if worker i purchased prescription antidepressant medication (ATC code N06 A) in year t, zero otherwise. definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. definition.value: Triple interaction of a female indicator, an indicator for being a parent (having a child younger than 19 living at home), and Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. Logs are taken in estimation, which drops 0.02% of observations. A LOWER bho means a greater need to work outside standard Danish business hours.

definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. claims.statement: Excluding the Global Financial Crisis years 2008-2009, a lower business hours overlap still raises the probability of purchasing antidepressants among women relative to men among college-educated workers under 45.

register_source.value: UH (foreign trade statistics register): all import and export transactions by 6-digit HS product code and partner country; worker-firm links from FIDA

definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. Logs are taken in estimation, which drops 0.02% of observations. A LOWER bho means a greater need to work outside standard Danish business hours.

timing.value: Firm's business hours overlap in the same year t as the outcome

outcome.label: Indicator variable indicating if the individual has purchased antidepressants in a given year

register_source.value: LMDB (prescription drugs register): purchases of prescription drugs by drug type (ATC codes); antidepressants = ATC N06 A

definition.value: Dummy equal to one if worker i purchased prescription antidepressant medication (ATC code N06 A) in year t, zero otherwise. Taken from the comprehensive prescription drugs register, which records all purchases of prescription drugs by drug type. Used as a proxy for mental well-being; Danish health care is free and universal, so access is not correlated with income or employment status.

timing.value: Purchases during year t, the same year as the firm's business hours overlap

units.value: change in the probability of purchasing antidepressants in a year (probability points, outcome is a 0/1 indicator) for women relative to men, per one unit of ln(business hours overlap); the paper notes ln(8)-ln(3) is approximately 1, so the coefficient is approximately the effect of a five-hour fall in overlap from 8 to 3 h

definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. definition.value: Interaction of the occupation-level O*NET index of limited temporal flexibility (the average of Time Pressure, Contact with others, Structured versus Unstructured Work, Freedom to Make Decisions and Establishing and Maintaining Interpersonal Relationships, standardized on the full sample, following Goldin 2014) with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. Logs are taken in estimation, which drops 0.02% of observations. A LOWER bho means a greater need to work outside standard Danish business hours. Each worker is assigned the characteristic of their first reported occupation in the data, so the index is time-invariant within a job spell.

treatment.label: Female × ln(bho trade) × O*NET (Contact with others)

register_source.value: O*NET occupational characteristics linked to ISCO codes from IDA; bho from UH (foreign trade statistics register)

definition.value: Triple interaction of a female indicator, Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. Logs are taken in estimation, which drops 0.02% of observations. A LOWER bho means a greater need to work outside standard Danish business hours. and the single standardized O*NET occupational characteristic 'Contact with others' of the worker's first reported occupation.

timing.value: Occupation characteristic fixed at first reported occupation; firm bho in year t

outcome.label: Indicator variable indicating if the individual has purchased antidepressants in a given year

register_source.value: LMDB (prescription drugs register): purchases of prescription drugs by drug type (ATC codes); antidepressants = ATC N06 A

definition.value: Dummy equal to one if worker i purchased prescription antidepressant medication (ATC code N06 A) in year t, zero otherwise. Taken from the comprehensive prescription drugs register, which records all purchases of prescription drugs by drug type. Used as a proxy for mental well-being; Danish health care is free and universal, so access is not correlated with income or employment status.

units.value: change in the probability of purchasing antidepressants (probability points) for women relative to men per unit of ln(business hours overlap) per standard deviation of the 'Contact with others' characteristic

definition.value: Interaction of an indicator for the worker being female with Natural log of the firm's trade-weighted business hours overlap, bho^trade_jt. For a partner country d, bho_d = max{8 - |UTC offset difference between Denmark and d|, 0}, i.e. the number of 9:00-17:00 working hours that overlap between Denmark and d (Eq. 1). The firm-level measure (Eq. 2) is the average of bho_d over the countries the firm traded with in year t, weighted by each country's share of the firm's total number of exported and imported 6-digit HS country-product combinations. Logs are taken in estimation, which drops 0.02% of observations. A LOWER bho means a greater need to work outside standard Danish business hours.

definition.value: Dummy equal to one if worker i purchased prescription antidepressant medication (ATC code N06 A) in year t, zero otherwise.
